views.name: ball_level_runs_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.bowler,
  COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
  COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0) AS extra_runs,
  COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0) AS total_runs_for_ball
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
  ON b.match_id = er.match_id
  AND b.over_id = er.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = er.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = er.innings_no
views.description: One row per ball (match_id, over_id, ball_id, innings_no, bowler) enriched with the batsman runs and extra runs for that ball, and a computed total_runs_for_ball (batsman runs + extra runs). Nulls for missing run values are normalized to 0 so totals can be summed safely.

views.name: over_level_runs_by_bowler
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  match_id,
  over_id,
  innings_no,
  bowler,
  SUM(total_runs_for_ball) AS runs_in_over
FROM
  ball_level_runs_enriched
GROUP BY
  match_id,
  over_id,
  innings_no,
  bowler
views.description: Aggregated runs conceded per over by bowler: one row per (match_id, over_id, innings_no, bowler) with sum of total runs in that over by that bowler. Uses ball-level enriched totals (batsman + extras).

views.name: match_level_max_over_runs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  olr.match_id,
  olr.innings_no,
  MAX(olr.runs_in_over) AS max_over_runs
FROM
  over_level_runs_by_bowler olr
GROUP BY
  olr.match_id,
  olr.innings_no
views.description: For each match (and innings), the maximum runs conceded in any single over within that match/innings. One row per match_id and innings_no exposing the max_over_runs value. This allows selecting over(s) in a match that tie for the match maximum.

views.name: delivery_level_runs_and_wicket
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.bowler AS bowler,
  COALESCE(SUM(bs.runs_scored), 0) AS runs_batsman,
  COALESCE(SUM(er.extra_runs), 0) AS runs_extras,
  COALESCE(SUM(bs.runs_scored), 0) + COALESCE(SUM(er.extra_runs), 0) AS runs_conceded,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(w.player_out) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS wicket_taken_flag
FROM
  ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN
  batsman_scored bs
  ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
LEFT JOIN
  extra_runs er
  ON b.match_id = er.match_id
  AND b.over_id = er.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = er.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = er.innings_no
LEFT JOIN
  wicket_taken w
  ON b.match_id = w.match_id
  AND b.over_id = w.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = w.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = w.innings_no
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.bowler
views.description: One row per delivered ball (match_id, over_id, ball_id, innings_no) with the bowler who delivered it, the summed batsman runs and summed extra runs for that delivery, total runs conceded on that delivery, and a flag indicating whether a wicket fell on that delivery. Treat missing batsman_scored or extra_runs rows as zero by aggregating them.

views.name: bowler_aggregate_per_match_delivery
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.bowler AS bowler,
  d.match_id AS match_id,
  d.over_id AS over_id,
  d.ball_id AS ball_id,
  d.innings_no AS innings_no,
  -- runs_conceded: prefer precomputed if delivery_level_runs_and_wicket exists, else sum batsman + extras
  COALESCE(d.runs_conceded, (COALESCE(d.runs_batsman, 0) + COALESCE(d.runs_extras, 0)), (COALESCE(bbr.total_runs_for_ball, 0))) AS runs_conceded,
  -- wicket_taken_flag: 1 if any wicket_taken record exists for this delivery, or if delivery-level flag provided
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(d.wicket_taken_flag, (CASE WHEN w.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) = 0 THEN 0
    ELSE 1
  END AS wicket_taken_flag
FROM
  -- prefer the richer joined delivery view if available
  delivery_level_runs_and_wicket d
LEFT JOIN
  wicket_taken w
ON
  d.match_id = w.match_id
  AND d.over_id = w.over_id
  AND d.ball_id = w.ball_id
  AND d.innings_no = w.innings_no
LEFT JOIN
  ball_level_runs_enriched bbr
ON
  d.match_id = bbr.match_id
  AND d.over_id = bbr.over_id
  AND d.ball_id = bbr.ball_id
  AND d.innings_no = bbr.innings_no
UNION
-- fallback: deliveries present in ball_level_runs_enriched but not in delivery_level_runs_and_wicket
SELECT
  bbr.bowler AS bowler,
  bbr.match_id AS match_id,
  bbr.over_id AS over_id,
  bbr.ball_id AS ball_id,
  bbr.innings_no AS innings_no,
  COALESCE(bbr.total_runs_for_ball, (COALESCE(bbr.runs_scored,0) + COALESCE(bbr.extra_runs,0))) AS runs_conceded,
  CASE WHEN w.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS wicket_taken_flag
FROM
  ball_level_runs_enriched bbr
LEFT JOIN
  delivery_level_runs_and_wicket d2
ON
  bbr.match_id = d2.match_id
  AND bbr.over_id = d2.over_id
  AND bbr.ball_id = d2.ball_id
  AND bbr.innings_no = d2.innings_no
LEFT JOIN
  wicket_taken w
ON
  bbr.match_id = w.match_id
  AND bbr.over_id = w.over_id
  AND bbr.ball_id = w.ball_id
  AND bbr.innings_no = w.innings_no
WHERE
  d2.match_id IS NULL
views.description: Aggregated measures per bowler at the granularity of bowler + delivery identifiers: pre-aggregates runs and wicket indicator for fast reuse when computing bowler totals. This view is grouped at (bowler, match_id, over_id, ball_id, innings_no) so it can be further aggregated to bowler-level metrics.

views.name: player_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player.player_id AS player_id,
  player.player_name AS player_name,
  player.country_name AS country_name,
  player.batting_hand AS batting_hand,
  player.bowling_skill AS bowling_skill,
  player.dob AS dob
FROM player
views.description: Canonical player reference with player_id and player_name for joins and display; exposes country and playing attributes for potential filters.
validated_on: Please help me find the names of top 5 players with the highest average runs per match in season 5, along with their batting averages.
counter_examples: Can you help me find the top 5 countries whose players have the highest average of their individual average runs per match across all seasons? Specifically, for each player, calculate their average runs per match over all matches they played, then compute the average of these player averages for each country, and include these country batting averages in the result.

views.name: ball_striker_link
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.striker
FROM
  ball_by_ball b
views.description: One row per ball delivery with the canonical striker (batsman on strike) and identifying ball keys, to allow joining ball events to the batsman who faced them.

views.name: batsman_runs_by_ball
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  bs.striker,
  b.runs_scored
FROM
  batsman_scored b
JOIN
  ball_striker_link bs
ON
  b.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
views.description: Batsman runs per ball: combine batsman_scored rows with the ball->striker mapping so each batsman_scored row is associated with the striker who faced that ball. Keeps all raw runs_scored rows for accurate summation even if multiple rows exist per ball.

views.name: player_match_total_runs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id AS match_id,
  b.striker AS player_id,
  SUM(b.runs_scored) AS total_runs
FROM
  batsman_runs_by_ball b
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.striker
views.description: Per-player-per-match total runs aggregated from batsman_runs_by_ball; one row per match and striker with the summed runs_scored. Useful as a reusable measure of a player's batting contribution in a specific match.

views.name: player_match_participation
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  match_id,
  player_id,
  team_id,
  role
FROM player_match
views.description: One row per player in a match recording which team they represented and their role in that match (denormalized from player_match). Useful as the canonical mapping of (match_id, player_id) -> team in that match.

views.name: ball_level_batsman_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.striker,
  r.runs_scored
FROM ball_striker_link AS b
LEFT JOIN batsman_runs_by_ball AS r
  ON b.match_id = r.match_id
  AND b.over_id = r.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = r.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = r.innings_no
  AND b.striker = r.striker
views.description: One row per ball delivery that captures which player was striker on that ball and the runs credited to the striker. This ties ball_by_ball to batsman_scored so each ball row includes the runs_scored for that delivery for the striker (NULL if no batsman_scored entry). Useful to compute player runs by summing across balls where they were the striker.

views.name: player_match_runs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.striker AS player_id,
  SUM(b.runs_scored) AS player_match_total_runs_in_that_match
FROM
  batsman_runs_by_ball b
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.striker
views.description: Aggregated runs per player per match across all innings: sums runs_scored for each player (as striker) within a match. One row per (match_id, player_id) with the total raw runs. Useful for queries needing player totals in a match (e.g., centuries).

views.name: balls_with_players_and_match
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  m.season_id AS "match.season_id",
  b.striker,
  bs.runs_scored
FROM ball_by_ball AS b
JOIN "match" AS m
  ON b.match_id = m.match_id
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS bs
  ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
views.description: One row per delivered ball, joining ball_by_ball with match to expose match season and ball-level batting player (striker) and runs from batsman_scored for that delivery. Keeps raw run events tied to the striker and match.
counter_examples: Can you help me find the top 5 countries whose players have the highest average of their individual average runs per match across all seasons? Specifically, for each player, calculate their average runs per match over all matches they played, then compute the average of these player averages for each country, and include these country batting averages in the result.

views.name: player_matches
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_id,
  match_id,
  team_id,
  role
FROM player_match
views.description: One row per player-match appearance from player_match. Indicates that a player participated in a match (and which team they represented). Useful to count matches played by player in a season after filtering matches.
counter_examples: Can you help me find the top 5 countries whose players have the highest average of their individual average runs per match across all seasons? Specifically, for each player, calculate their average runs per match over all matches they played, then compute the average of these player averages for each country, and include these country batting averages in the result.

views.name: over_batsman_runs_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  SUM(b.runs_scored) AS batsman_runs
FROM
  batsman_scored b
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id
views.description: Sum of batsman runs grouped at the granularity of match_id, innings_no, over_id (one row per over) — missing rows imply zero runs in the final query logic.

views.name: over_extra_runs_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  er.match_id,
  er.innings_no,
  er.over_id,
  SUM(COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0)) AS extra_runs
FROM extra_runs er
GROUP BY
  er.match_id,
  er.innings_no,
  er.over_id
views.description: Sum of extra runs grouped at the granularity of match_id, innings_no, over_id (one row per over) — missing rows imply zero extra runs in the final query logic.

views.name: over_bowler_lookup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  MIN(b.bowler) AS bowler
FROM
  ball_by_ball b
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id
views.description: One representative bowler (player id) for each over identified by match_id, innings_no, over_id. If multiple ball_by_ball rows exist for the same over, this view returns one row per over (any single bowler value) so the over can be attributed to a bowler.

views.name: match_season
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.match_id,
  m.season_id,
  m.match_date,
  m.team_1,
  m.team_2
FROM match AS m
views.description: One row per match with its season_id and core match identifiers to allow joins from event-level tables (ball_by_ball, batsman_scored, wicket_taken) to season. Normalizes match basic attributes needed for season-level grouping.

views.name: batsman_runs_per_match_player
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bs.match_id,
  bb.striker AS player_id,
  SUM(bs.runs_scored) AS runs_in_match
FROM
  batsman_scored bs
JOIN
  ball_striker_link bb
  ON bs.match_id = bb.match_id
  AND bs.over_id = bb.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = bb.ball_id
  AND bs.innings_no = bb.innings_no
GROUP BY
  bs.match_id,
  bb.striker
views.description: Per match and per batsman (player) the total raw runs scored computed from batsman_scored rows. Keeps one row per (match_id, player_id) so higher-level aggregations (e.g., per-season per-batsman) can be computed by summing runs over matches joined to match_season.

views.name: bowler_wickets_per_match_player
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  wt.match_id AS match_id,
  b.bowler AS bowler_id,
  COUNT(*) AS wickets_in_match
FROM wicket_taken wt
JOIN ball_by_ball b
  ON wt.match_id = b.match_id
  AND wt.over_id = b.over_id
  AND wt.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND wt.innings_no = b.innings_no
WHERE wt.kind_out NOT IN ('run out', 'hit wicket', 'retired hurt')
GROUP BY wt.match_id, b.bowler

semantic_filters.kind_out_exclude: run out, hit wicket, retired hurt

views.description: Per match and per bowler (player) the raw wicket count from wicket_taken rows, excluding non-bowler dismissals (run out, hit wicket, retired hurt). One row per (match_id, bowler_id) for use in season-level aggregations.

views.name: ball_bat_pair_by_delivery
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  bb.striker,
  b.non_striker,
  bs.runs_scored
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN ball_striker_link bb
  ON b.match_id = bb.match_id
  AND b.over_id = bb.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bb.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = bb.innings_no
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
views.description: One row per ball delivery (match/innings/over/ball) with the two batsmen on crease (striker and non_striker) and the batsman runs on that delivery. Normalizes ball_by_ball joined to batsman_scored to produce canonical delivery-level records.

views.name: partnership_runs_by_pair_innings
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  CASE WHEN b.striker <= b.non_striker THEN b.striker ELSE b.non_striker END AS player_a_id,
  CASE WHEN b.striker <= b.non_striker THEN b.non_striker ELSE b.striker END AS player_b_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN b.striker <= b.non_striker THEN b.runs_scored ELSE 0 END) AS player_a_runs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN b.striker <= b.non_striker THEN 0 ELSE b.runs_scored END) AS player_b_runs,
  SUM(b.runs_scored) AS partnership_runs
FROM
  ball_bat_pair_by_delivery b
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  player_a_id,
  player_b_id
views.description: Partnership-level aggregated runs for each unordered pair of batsmen within a single match innings. Aggregates delivery-level batsman runs to compute total runs contributed by each batsman in the partnership and total partnership runs. The pair is canonicalized so player_a_id <= player_b_id to represent unordered pair.

views.name: match_level_max_partnership
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.match_id,
  MAX(p.partnership_runs) AS max_partnership_runs
FROM partnership_runs_by_pair_innings p
GROUP BY p.match_id
views.description: For each match, compute the maximum partnership_runs observed in that match (across all innings and unordered batsman pairs). Useful to filter partnerships that equal the match maximum.

views.name: ball_delivery_with_extras_and_bowler
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.bowler,
  b.team_bowling,
  b.striker,
  COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
  er.extra_type,
  er.extra_runs
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
  ON er.match_id = b.match_id
  AND er.over_id = b.over_id
  AND er.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND er.innings_no = b.innings_no
views.description: One row per individual delivery (match/innings/over/ball) joined to ball_by_ball, extra_runs (if any) and batsman_scored to expose bowler, legal/illegal flag, and runs scored by batsman on that delivery.

views.name: bowler_wicket_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  w.match_id,
  w.innings_no,
  w.over_id,
  w.ball_id,
  w.player_out,
  w.kind_out
FROM wicket_taken AS w
JOIN ball_by_ball AS b
  ON b.match_id = w.match_id
  AND b.over_id = w.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = w.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = w.innings_no
WHERE lower(w.kind_out) != 'run out'
  AND lower(w.kind_out) NOT IN ('recharge','retired hurt','obstructing the field','handled the ball')

semantic_filters.kind_out: exclude 'run out' and other non-bowler-attributed kinds

views.description: One row per wicket event (from wicket_taken) filtered/flagged to indicate whether the dismissal is credited to the bowler (exclude run outs and other non-bowler-attributed kinds). Includes the match identifiers and player credited as wicket taker (player_out is the dismissed player; bowler attribution will be joined via ball_delivery).

views.name: per_bowler_per_match_raw_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.bowler AS bowler,
  COUNT(*) AS total_balls_incl_illegal,
  SUM(CASE
        WHEN e.extra_type IN ('wides','noballs') THEN 0
        ELSE 1
      END) AS legal_balls,
  SUM(COALESCE(bs.runs_scored,0)) AS runs_conceded_off_bat,
  SUM(CASE WHEN w.kind_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_attributed
FROM ball_delivery_with_extras_and_bowler b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
LEFT JOIN extra_runs e
  ON e.match_id = b.match_id
  AND e.over_id = b.over_id
  AND e.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND e.innings_no = b.innings_no
LEFT JOIN bowler_wicket_events w
  ON w.match_id = b.match_id
  AND w.over_id = b.over_id
  AND w.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND w.innings_no = b.innings_no
GROUP BY
  b.bowler,
  b.match_id
views.description: Aggregated raw measures per bowler per match: total deliveries bowled (legal and total), total legal balls (excluding wides/noballs), runs conceded off the bat (sum of batsman_scored.runs_scored for deliveries bowled by that bowler), and wickets credited to that bowler (count of wicket events with kinds attributed to bowler). This is raw aggregation; final rates and best-match selection are computed from this view.
